```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

# choose ozone unit "ppm" or "ppb"
o3_unit <- "ppm"
```


```{r, message = FALSE}
# Purpose: process a single year of data to output clean dataframe
# Argument: file_path - file path of the dataset
# Argument: o3_unit - unit of ozone; ppm by default
# Return: clean dataframe, ready for analysis
process_aq <- function(file_path, unit = o3_unit) {
  # read in and clean data
  clean_data <- read_csv(file_path) |>
    # format date correctly
    mutate(Date = mdy(Date)) |>
    # rename columns
    rename(
      co = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      pm25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      ozone = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    ) |>
    # drop unit columns
    select(Date, co, pm25, ozone) |>
    # drop duplicates
    distinct() |>
    # daily averages if multiple measurements for same day
    group_by(Date) |>
    summarize(
      co = mean(co, na.rm = TRUE),
      pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
      ozone = mean(ozone, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    # negative pollutants to 0
    mutate(across(c(co, pm25, ozone), ~ pmax(.x, 0, na.rm = TRUE)))

  # ozone ppb option
  if (unit == "ppb") {
    clean_data <- clean_data |>
      mutate(ozone = ozone * 1000)
  } else if (unit != "ppm") {
    stop("Invalid unit argument. Please choose either 'ppm' or 'ppb'.")
  }

  # return clean data
  return(clean_data)
}

# run function on each dataset
clean_2018 <- process_aq("data/AQ_2018.csv", o3_unit)
clean_2019 <- process_aq("data/AQ_2019.csv", o3_unit)
clean_2020 <- process_aq("data/AQ_2020.csv", o3_unit)

# combine into single dataset
all_years_data <- bind_rows(clean_2018, clean_2019, clean_2020)
```

## Minimum and Maximum Pollutants for Each Year
```{r}
# Purpose: make table for a single year, showing min/max for each pollutant
# Argument: df - clean data frame
# Argument: year_label - the year
# Return: clean table
create_summary_table <- function(df, year_label, unit = o3_unit) {
  df |>
    # calculate the min/max for each pollutant, rounding to 3 decimals
    summarize(
      CO_min = round(min(co, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      CO_max = round(max(co, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      PM25_min = round(min(pm25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      PM25_max = round(max(pm25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      O3_min = round(min(ozone, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      O3_max = round(max(ozone, na.rm = TRUE), 3)
    ) |>
    # reshape the wide summary statistics into a long format
    pivot_longer(
      cols = everything(),
      names_to = c("Pollutant", "Statistic"),
      names_sep = "_"
    ) |>
    # reshape back so min and max become columns and pollutants become rows
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Statistic,
      values_from = value
    ) |>
    # assign clear, informative row names that include measurement units
    mutate(Pollutant = c(
      "Carbon Monoxide (ppm)",
      "PM2.5 (µg/m³ LC)",
      paste0("Ozone (", unit, ")")
    )) |>
    # initialize the gt table and add professional headers and labels
    gt() |>
    cols_label(
      Pollutant = "Pollutant and Units",
      min = "Minimum Daily Concentration",
      max = "Maximum Daily Concentration"
    ) |>
    tab_header(
      title = paste("Daily Air Quality Summary - ", year_label)
    )
}
```

```{r}
# 2018 min/max pollutants
create_summary_table(clean_2018, 2018, o3_unit)
```
&nbsp;

```{r}
# 2019 min/max pollutants
create_summary_table(clean_2019, 2019, o3_unit)
```
&nbsp;

```{r}
# 2020 min/max pollutants
create_summary_table(clean_2020, 2020, o3_unit)
```

## Carbon Monoxide and Ozone by Month
```{r}
# calculate monthly mean, SD, sample size, and 95% CI for CO and Ozone
monthly_stats <- all_years_data |>
  # get month from Date column
  mutate(Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(Month) |>
  summarise(
    # --- Carbon Monoxide (CO) stats ---
    co_mean = mean(co, na.rm = TRUE),
    co_sd = sd(co, na.rm = TRUE),
    co_n = sum(!is.na(co)), # number of non-missing days
    co_ci = 1.96 * (co_sd / sqrt(co_n)), # margin of error
    co_lower = co_mean - co_ci, # CI lower bound
    co_upper = co_mean + co_ci, # CI upper bound

    # --- Ozone (O3) stats ---
    o3_mean = mean(ozone, na.rm = TRUE),
    o3_sd = sd(ozone, na.rm = TRUE),
    o3_n = sum(!is.na(ozone)), # number of non-missing days
    o3_ci = 1.96 * (o3_sd / sqrt(o3_n)), # margin of error
    o3_lower = o3_mean - o3_ci, # CI lower bound
    o3_upper = o3_mean + o3_ci, # CI upper bound

    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# reshape the summary statistics into a long format for ggplot
monthly_long <- monthly_stats |>
  # Stack co_mean and o3_mean into a single column called 'Mean'
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co_mean, o3_mean),
    names_to = "Pollutant",
    values_to = "Mean"
  ) |>
  # Assign the correct lower and upper CI bounds depending on the pollutant
  mutate(
    Lower = if_else(Pollutant == "co_mean",
      co_lower,
      o3_lower
    ),
    Upper = if_else(Pollutant == "co_mean",
      co_upper,
      o3_upper
    ),
    # Rename the pollutant codes into clean, readable labels for the plot
    Pollutant = if_else(Pollutant == "co_mean",
      "Carbon Monoxide (CO)",
      paste0("Ozone (O3) [", o3_unit, "]")
    )
  ) |>
  # Keep only the columns needed for plotting
  select(Month, Pollutant, Mean, Lower, Upper)
```

```{r}
# colors for ggplot
ozone_label <- paste0("Ozone (O3) [", o3_unit, "]")
color_map <- c("darkblue", "hotpink")
names(color_map) <- c("Carbon Monoxide (CO)", ozone_label)

# create the ggplot visualization for Plot 1
ggplot(monthly_long, aes(x = Month, y = Mean, color = Pollutant)) +
  # add points to display the monthly mean concentrations
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # error bars for 95% CIs using our Lower and Upper bounds
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_map) +
  # CO and Ozone will have independent y-axes
  facet_wrap(~Pollutant, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  # add labels
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average Air Quality Trends (2018–2020)",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Concentration (CO in ppm, Ozone in specified unit)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  # hide the legend
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )
```

Because carbon monoxide and ozone are measured on very different scales, independent y-axes (scales = "free_y" in the facet_wrap function) were used for each pollutant to ensure the patterns in both pollutants are readable.

## $PM_{2.5}$ by Month and Year
```{r}
# prepare monthly data PM2.5 grouped by year and month
pm25_monthly <- all_years_data |>
  # extract month and year
  mutate(
    Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
    Year = factor(year(Date))
  ) |>
  # calculate mean for each month in each year
  group_by(Year, Month) |>
  summarize(
    pm25_mean = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# create the ggplot visualization for Plot 2
ggplot(
  pm25_monthly,
  aes(x = Month, y = pm25_mean, color = Year, group = Year)
) +
  # connecting lines
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  # points to show each monthly mean value
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  # colors for each year
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "2018" = "darkblue",
    "2019" = "darkorange",
    "2020" = "hotpink"
  )) +
  # labels
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average PM2.5 Concentration",
    y = "PM2.5 Concentration (µg/m³ LC)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )
```

I used `geom_line` to show how the $PM_{2.5}$ concentration changed throughout the year, and I combined it with `geom_point` to make each month stand out.

## Interpretation
While interpreting, I kept in mind that 2020 only has data until the end of April.

* According to the tables, maximum daily concentration of $PM_{2.5}$ increased by almost 10 units from 2019 to 2020, compared to 1 unit increase from 2018 to 2020.
* According to the plot of $CO$ and $O_3$ by month, they are opposite of each other: carbon monoxide decreases then increases throughout the year, and ozone increases then decreases throughout the year.
* According to the $PM_{2.5}$ plot, while the peak concentrations vary across years and 2019 fluctuates, the annual lows consistently occur during the late summer and early fall months (at least for 2018 and 2019).
